sources.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, extended and corrected Summer 2016 lecture notes, arXiv:1311.2717v2
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 157-page PDF. Read the full relevant KMS section §3.4, printed pp. 74–78 (PDF pages 74–78): Definition 3.4.4, Proposition 3.4.5, finite Gibbs/KMS and uniqueness discussion, and Corollary 3.4.9. The complete PDF was previously retrieved into research/physics-remaining-80-2026-10-17-batch-39-sources/raw/ and its exact bytes/hash were re-inspected; unrelated chapters were not claimed as read.

contents.name: §3.4, Definition 3.4.4, printed p. 74: physical-time KMS strip and reversed upper boundary
contents.support: The notes use the closed strip of width ħβ and the same lower/upper correlation order. They later set ħ=1; this item retains physical seconds explicitly.

contents.name: §3.4, finite Gibbs calculation and matrix-unit uniqueness discussion, printed pp. 76–77
contents.support: The source gives the finite Gibbs strip identity and sketches uniqueness through matrix units. The item supplies the full finite-dimensional derivation, including degeneracies and the one-dimensional case.

contents.name: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.9 and finite Gibbs limit discussion, printed pp. 77–78
contents.support: The source motivates finite-volume Gibbs limits as a route to KMS states; this local lemma supplies the explicit trace extension, state compactness, derivative bound, and closed-strip convergence under the stated finite-range assumptions.

contents.name: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.9: existence of infinite spin KMS states, printed pp. 77–78
contents.support: The source states the existence conclusion for its strictly local bounded interaction framework. The item proves the exact local-pair limit and all-observable norm extension under its explicit conditional finite-matrix interfaces.

contents.name: §3.4, finite Gibbs boundary example, printed pp. 76–77
contents.support: The two-level example is a direct finite-matrix specialization of the source Gibbs/KMS calculation and checks the physical-time exponential sign explicitly.

contents.name: §3.4, Proposition 3.4.5, printed/PDF p. 74: evaluation of KMS strip functions on entire analytic elements
contents.reason: As already explicitly recorded in the native source-reading table, the assigned bounded-strip proofs do not invoke the general entire-analytic-element evaluation theorem or its density machinery. Finite matrices have explicit entire exponential entries and their strip identity is proved directly; infinite local-pair limits use closed-strip compactness and real-time generator bounds instead. No general entire-element theorem is claimed.

contents.name: §3.4, Theorem 3.4.6 (Roepstorff–Araki–Sewell), printed/PDF p. 75: KMS equivalent to a derivation/logarithmic inequality
contents.reason: The assigned pair proves bounded-strip KMS statements directly at fixed beta>0. It does not claim the general equivalence with the generator-domain logarithmic inequality, its zero-denominator conventions, or the inverse implication. None of its proofs invokes this theorem.

contents.name: §3.4, Proposition 3.4.7, printed/PDF pp. 75–76: limits for varying dynamics and inverse temperatures, including beta=+infinity
contents.reason: The general theorem permits varying inverse temperatures and a ground-state limit, with its own generator-convergence hypotheses. The assigned lem-qsm-gibbs-strip-limit proves its fixed positive-beta finite-range local-pair case directly by state compactness and closed-strip estimates; it neither invokes nor proves the broader proposition.

contents.name: §3.4, Exercise 3.4.8, printed/PDF p. 76: every finite-matrix tracial linear functional is a scalar multiple of the trace
contents.reason: The general tracial-functional classification is not asserted by the assigned pair. The finite KMS characterization derives off-diagonal vanishing and diagonal Gibbs ratios directly with matrix units, so it does not require the separate exercise or a general tracial-functional lemma.

contents.name: §3.4, Remark 3.4.10, printed/PDF p. 78: more general convergence hypotheses for KMS-limit constructions
contents.reason: The assigned interaction scope is uniformly bounded finite range, with the exact selected thermodynamic dynamics and local generator. It does not assert the broader varying-domain or approximate-generator convergence generalization in this remark.

contents.name: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.9, printed/PDF p. 77: nonempty ground-state set (separate second conclusion)
contents.reason: Only the fixed beta>0 KMS-existence conclusion is covered inline by thm-qsm-infinite-spin-kms-existence. Ground states, beta=+infinity, and their separate existence criterion are outside this approved KMS pair; no ground-state theorem is inferred from the positive-temperature strip proof.

sources.title: David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, complete author-hosted lecture notes, arXiv:math-ph/0107009v1
sources.locator: Complete 36-page author-hosted PDF, dated 11 July 2001. Current scoped local-PDF check: Chapter 1 §7 KMS theorem, invariance, bound and time-rescaling convention are on printed/PDF pp. 13–14; Chapter 2 §6 finite local Gibbs definition and limit-point existence are on p. 24, and the general infinite-spin Gibbs/KMS equivalence statement (citing Bratteli–Robinson) is on p. 25. That general theorem is not a finite-matrix uniqueness proof. The finite characterization is proved locally and supported independently by Naaijkens pp. 76–77. No new fetch or external source rereading is claimed.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, KMS condition theorem, printed pp. 13–14: analytic strip boundary identity, invariance and norm bound
contents.support: The notes state that the KMS condition implies invariance and the correlation norm bound. This item supplies the full periodic-gluing, Morera, and Liouville proof rather than taking the consequence on authority.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, analytic-strip KMS definition, printed p. 13
contents.support: The abstract strip convention agrees after the source’s stated time rescaling and ħ=1 convention; the authored definition fixes βħ seconds and states boundedness explicitly.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, local Gibbs states and Gibbs/KMS discussion, printed pp. 24–25
contents.support: The source constructs local Gibbs states and records that limit points are KMS under an exponentially summable interaction condition. The item gives the finite-range specialization with its full conditional compactness and strip-limit argument.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, finite local Gibbs density definition (p. 24), with related general Gibbs/KMS context (p. 25)
contents.support: The source defines finite local Gibbs densities on p. 24 and states a general infinite-spin Gibbs/KMS equivalence theorem on p. 25, citing Bratteli–Robinson. It does not itself provide the local finite matrix-unit uniqueness proof. The assigned finite theorem proves both directions directly and has independent Naaijkens pp. 76–77 support; this source supplies related Gibbs/KMS context only.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, KMS strip correlation bound, printed p. 13
contents.support: The source records the uniform correlation bound for the KMS strip condition. The item proves the required closed-strip estimate and lower-edge uniqueness directly from the imported Hadamard three-lines theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, finite-time Gibbs/KMS convention, printed pp. 13–14
contents.support: The source gives the finite Gibbs/KMS convention in a rescaled time variable. The example checks the same boundary relation with explicit SI units and physical time.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, lemma on norm-density of entire analytic elements, printed/PDF p. 13
contents.reason: The assigned infinite-spin arguments use bounded strip functions, local real-time generator bounds and norm density of the strictly local algebra. They do not invoke or prove the general density of entire analytic elements or its Gaussian convolution construction; finite matrix exponentials are treated explicitly.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, theorem on equivalence of infinite-spin Gibbs and KMS states under exponential summability, printed/PDF p. 25
contents.reason: This general equivalence is stated by Ruelle with proof referred to Bratteli–Robinson. The assigned pair proves finite matrix Gibbs/KMS characterization and fixed-beta finite-range infinite KMS existence, not the converse infinite Gibbs characterization, perturbative Gibbs definition or general exponential-summability equivalence.
